record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: Does there exist a locally compact countable dense homogeneous space that has a dense open subspace which is not countable dense homogeneous?

evidence.quote: Problem 9 (Ungar). Is there a locally compact CDH-space with a dense open non-CDH-subspace?

artifact.self_contained_problem: A topological space $X$ is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for every pair of countable dense subsets $A, B \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h \colon X \to X$ such that $h(A) = B$. Question: Does there exist a locally compact (Hausdorff) countable dense homogeneous space $X$ that contains a dense open subspace $U \subseteq X$ which fails to be countable dense homogeneous?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is attributed to Ungar and listed as an open problem in surveys on countable dense homogeneity. A web search found related work by Hrušák and van Mill on nearly CDH spaces but no resolution of this specific question; it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Nearly Countable Dense Homogeneous Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses CDH spaces and references Ungar's work; no resolution of the locally compact dense open non-CDH subspace problem is given.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature on CDH spaces does not record a solution to Ungar's question.
